title: A place-based sports intervention is being used as a bridge from social connection to mental-health literacy, aspiration and re-engagement for boys and young men at risk of isolation
source_unit: UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport, Rugby League Cares and Edge Hill University, evaluation of Offload and Movember Ahead of the Game pilots
geography: Wigan and Wakefield, England; boys and young men experiencing loneliness, isolation or NEET status

denominator.unit: more than 1,400 participants reported as engaged across the two pilot programmes

delivery_partners.unit: Community Club Organisations linked to professional rugby league teams delivering the pilots

programme_pair.value: Movember Ahead of the Game and Offload

observations.method: Government-funded pilot delivery by Rugby League Cares with independent evaluation commissioned from Edge Hill University's Centre for Mental Health, Sport and Physical Activity Research and Faculty of Education.
observations.uncertainty: The public summary reports programme reach but does not establish a randomized comparison, representative reach, retention, effect size or long-term outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Boys aged 11–18 in the prevention programme and NEET young men aged 16–24 in the targeted programme.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported reach can include varied levels of engagement and does not show that every participant experienced improved connection, wellbeing or aspiration.

observations.period: November 2025–March 2026; programme design and target populations

ahead_of_game.value: prevention programme for boys and young men aged 11–18 and trusted adults, teaching mental-health conversation and support skills

offload.value: six-week early-intervention behaviour-change programme for NEET young men aged 16–24 focused on social connections, wellbeing, aspirations and coping with life challenges

trusted_network.value: parents, guardians, youth workers, group leaders and volunteers are included as part of the support network

observations.method: Programme description and evaluation scope from the UK government publication and Edge Hill University report abstract.
observations.uncertainty: Programme descriptions indicate intended mechanisms, not evidence that the mechanisms were delivered uniformly or caused observed changes.
observations.subgroup: Boys and young men at different prevention and early-intervention stages, including NEET young men and their trusted adults.
observations.counterinterpretation: A single sports identity may be a strong engagement hook for some participants but exclude those who do not identify with rugby, sport or male-coded group settings.

observations.period: 2026 evaluation; social connection, wellbeing and aspiration outcomes

denominator.unit: independent evaluation of the two pilot programme models

evaluation_questions.value: whether the programmes improve social connections, wellbeing and aspirations, and what should be adapted for future scale-up

reported_direction.value: public summaries describe encouraging improvements in social connection, wellbeing and aspirations among participants

scale_up_question.value: evaluation is intended to generate actionable learning for potential future scale-up or adaptation

observations.method: Independent evaluation commissioned by Rugby League Cares and reported through UK government, Edge Hill University and partner summaries.
observations.uncertainty: The accessible public summaries do not provide complete outcome tables, comparison groups, attrition, measurement instruments or effect sizes; reported improvement should not be treated as causal proof.
observations.subgroup: Pilot participants, delivery organizations, trusted adults, community-sport practitioners and policymakers considering youth loneliness interventions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Positive change may reflect selection into the programme, intensive local delivery, novelty, regression to the mean, participant self-report or concurrent support.

observations.period: 2026; place-based community sport as a social-infrastructure mechanism

engagement_hook.value: professional-sport identity and trusted community organizations are used to lower the barrier to joining conversations about mental health and connection

reengagement_route.value: regular group activity is linked in the programme logic to confidence, coping, aspirations and possible re-engagement with education or employment

local_system.value: four club-community foundations create a place-based delivery network rather than a purely digital or clinical intervention

observations.method: Synthesis of pilot design, public evaluation summaries and the broader DCMS social-connection evidence base.
observations.uncertainty: The mechanism is plausible and locally grounded but not independently established across places, sports, genders, cultures or delivery organizations.
observations.subgroup: Young people with weak social ties, NEET young men, local community organizations, sports foundations, schools, youth services and employment support.
observations.counterinterpretation: Sports-based delivery can reproduce exclusion, require transport and time, or prioritize visible group participation over quieter forms of connection and support.

related_sources.claim: Edge Hill University abstract and evaluation scope.
UK policy framework connecting the pilot to wider youth social-connection policy.

boundary: This record adds a named intervention and evaluation route to the youth-belonging sequence. It is a local pilot with public summary findings, not a randomized trial, national programme evaluation, clinical treatment study, or proof that sport-based connection scales uniformly.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official GOV.UK publication, Edge Hill University abstract and university report page were reviewed for pilot locations, timing, reach, programme populations, delivery model, evaluation questions, reported direction and limits; the GOV.UK publication page was hashed.
